properties.description:
During the summer of 2023, contact between vessels and the pier facility operated by Pacific Terminals, Inc, sustained significant structural damage to the pier structure rendering a portion of it unusable for business purposes. The impact damaged  two 14" fender piles, two HDPE chaffing plates and detached these pilings from the exisitng piling cap.

The damage has rendered approximately 20 lineal feet of the berth unusable for business. Repairs must be conducted as soon as possible to be included in the present fish window and minimize lost revenue. 

Pacific Terminals is proposing to replace the following items at the Terminal 7 dock due to damage from a recent vessel impact;
-Pull and replace two existing damaged 14" fender timber piles with 14" steel or UHMW/HDPE or similar poly-coated timber pile
- Pull and replace two HDPE chaffing plates on newly installed fender piles
-Reattach all replaced pilings to replaced piling caps with galvanized hardware

It is a mixed-use retail and 100% Affordable Housing project that is on the Priority 2 list. Mechanical and electrical upgrades include new exhaust fans, new heat pumps for heating and cooling, low flow plumbing fixtures, new all building hot and cold water plumbing system, all LED lighting, a new fire sprinkler system, a new fire alarm system. Interior improvements include new cabinets and counter tops, Energy Star appliances, tubs/showers, new flooring, base, and paint throughout. cold shell for the commercial spaces. All new insulation on entire exterior envelope as part of the work. We are looking at 36 family sized units over retail/restaurant space.

properties.description:
The proposed project is to convert an existing 1 story, 5400sf mortuary building into the new home for the Rainier Valley Food Bank. 

The scope of work includes expanding and remodeling the existing building to allow food bank programs and operations to move in. Proposed spaces and alterations the design team is considering include: adding an interior or exterior walk-in cooler and a walk-in freezer; converting the existing lobby into a commercial kitchen with walk-up to-go window; adding a larger entry canopy; converting a large room into a grocery store-like distribution space; adding a small mezzanine; adding a loading dock; converting some existing parking spaces into a garden and waste enclosure; expand the building toward Rainier Ave by ~3900sf for additional office and staff support spaces.
There is also interest to activate and occupy the site with a temporary food village during the design, permitting, and construction process.

properties.description:
Proposed Project.  Arky Vandelay LLC (the "Applicant") has leased space located at 2214 1st Avenue, Seattle, WA 98121 (the "Premises") to operate a retail marijuana store.  The location complies with all city and state regulations governing the location of marijuana retail stores.  The lease is for a five-year term with rent at over $18,000 per month.  

The Applicant applied for and received approval from the Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board (the "LCB") to move its marijuana retail license (License No. 414450, hereinafter the "License") from 417 NW 65th St. ("Prior Location") to the Premises.  Per the LCB's requirements, as of October 22, 2020, Applicant closed operations at the Prior Location.   The License is now tied to the Premises, and Applicant has been paying rent for six months without any revenue to cover those losses.  

	The Ordinance From Which A Variance Is Requested.  While fully licensed by the LCB, the Applicant is unable to operate its licensed marijuana retail at the Premises in Belltown because it is unable to secure its City of Seattle (the "City") marijuana retail license. The problem is the City's strict application of SMC 23.42.058.C.5, despite the fact that the City's strict application of SMC 23.42.058.C.5 contradicts the plain meaning and reasonable application of SMC 23.42.058.C.6.  This contradiction is more fully explained below.

Three months after the LCB approved of the Applicant's License at the Premises, Washington OG, LLC ("Washington OG") obtained approval to move its marijuana retail license (License #431327) to 2114 Western Avenue, Suite B.  While the location satisfies the requirements of WAC 314-55-050(10), the location is basically a windowless closet tucked away in the second story of a building.  As such, Washington OG is not likely to ever receive a certificate of occupancy from the City or otherwise be allowed to operate a retail store at 2114 Western Avenue, Suite B.  With no means to legally sell cannabis products there, the location cannot be considered a property with existing major marijuana activity (explained below).

Even though the Applicant was approved first by the LCB, and is ready, able, and willing to operate at the Premises, the Applicant cannot open for business without obtaining a variance to SMC 23.42.058.C.5.  That is because the City is treating Washington OG's premises, which was licensed three months after Applicant's Premises, as a second property in Belltown with major marijuana activity, thereby blocking Applicant from opening.  Applicant seeks a variance to avoid this unjust and unintended result.

properties.description:
General Recycling of Washington needs to maintain the dock at their facility on the Duwamish River. This includes replacing up to ten 12-inch fender piles each year, and other minor repairs , such as replacing pile caps, surfacing repairs, and whaler and caulk replacement, over the next five years (October 2017- February 2023). Bent steel or damaged wood fender piles will be replaced with 12-inch diameter steel piles. Piles will be removed and replaced using a vibratory hammer (no impact driving will occur). Pile driving activities are expected to occur over a maximum of three weeks in any given year. Pile driving is expected to take three to five days  during that three weeks. All work will occur in the Duwamish River near the dock. Equipment and materials will be brought in via barge. The barge(s) will be anchored using spud piles. A staging and sequencing plan will be developed with the contractor. In-water work will adhere to agency-approved (WDFW and USACE) work windows.
In order to minimize temporary impacts to the aquatic environment, work below the ordinary high water mark (OHWM) is proposed to occur between October and February of each year.
